title: PowerShell repeatedly spawns hostname.exe + whoami.exe back-to-back (host/user discovery)
source: ML-style review of Wazuh archives.json (events with no corresponding alerts.json entry)
description: 48 Sysmon EID 1 events: powershell.exe (HVAN\Administrator) launches HOSTNAME.EXE then whoami.exe within <1 s, repeated once per atomic test (every ~30-40 s). It is the Invoke-AtomicRedTeam test-logging prologue but, from a detection view, is a recurring discovery pair run by an interactive PowerShell with no associated alert. Note the separate `cmd /c whoami /all` was alerted (92032) but plain whoami.exe launched directly by powershell.exe was not.
why_wazuh_missed: Wazuh 92xxx rules only fire for whoami/hostname when wrapped by cmd.exe; direct PowerShell child process of these LOLBins is not covered. Likely also low-severity/noisy so no default rule.
detection_hints_for_rule: Sysmon EID 1: parentImage endswith \powershell.exe AND image endswith \whoami.exe (commandLine without cmd.exe wrapper)
Sysmon EID 1: image endswith \HOSTNAME.EXE with parentImage endswith \powershell.exe
Correlation: HOSTNAME.EXE and whoami.exe with same parentProcessGuid within 2 s, >=3 occurrences in 10 min (frequency / timeframe rule)
